topic: Decide on a policy for remote versus in-office work days

scenario.topic: Decide on a policy for remote versus in-office work days
scenario.opening_question: How should we balance remote and in-office days to keep productivity and team connection strong?

options.name: Fixed Two Days In-Office Weekly
options.upside: Ensures regular face-to-face collaboration twice a week.
options.tradeoff: Limits flexibility for employees who prefer more remote work.
options.concern: Some may find commuting twice a week disruptive or costly.

options.name: Flexible Choice With Mandatory Core Hours
options.upside: Maximizes individual flexibility while ensuring overlap for meetings.
options.tradeoff: Less predictable in-office presence may reduce spontaneous collaboration.
options.concern: Core hours may not suit all time zones or personal schedules.
options.best_for: Teams valuing flexibility with some guaranteed overlap.

options.name: Three Consecutive In-Office Days Weekly
options.upside: Concentrates in-person work for deeper collaboration and project focus.
options.tradeoff: Longer consecutive commute may cause fatigue or scheduling conflicts.
options.concern: Less flexibility for personal appointments during in-office stretch.
options.best_for: Teams needing blocks of in-person collaboration.

options.name: Fully Remote With Quarterly Office Meetups
options.upside: Maximizes remote work flexibility and reduces daily commute stress.
options.tradeoff: Less frequent in-person interaction may weaken team bonds.
options.concern: Quarterly meetups may be costly and inconvenient for some.
options.best_for: Teams prioritizing remote flexibility with occasional face time.

shared_context: The company supports flexible work but wants clear guidelines.
The goal is to maintain collaboration while respecting personal work preferences.

For this simulated decision, I’ll treat the following setup as the shared facts.
Options:
A) Fixed Two Days In-Office Weekly — commute requirement: Mandatory on in-office days; in office days per week: 2; meeting days: In-office days only (+ Ensures regular face-to-face collaboration twice a week; − Limits flexibility for employees who prefer more remote work)
B) Flexible Choice With Mandatory Core Hours — core hours: 10am-3pm daily; in office days per week: Employee choice; meeting days: Any day during core hours (+ Maximizes individual flexibility while ensuring overlap for meetings; − Less predictable in-office presence may reduce spontaneous collaboration)
C) Three Consecutive In-Office Days Weekly — commute requirement: Mandatory on in-office days; in office days per week: 3; meeting days: In-office days preferred (+ Concentrates in-person work for deeper collaboration and project focus; − Longer consecutive commute may cause fatigue or scheduling conflicts)
D) Fully Remote With Quarterly Office Meetups — travel budget: Company covers meetup travel; in office days per week: 0; office meetups per year: 4 (+ Maximizes remote work flexibility and reduces daily commute stress; − Less frequent in-person interaction may weaken team bonds)

How should we balance remote and in-office days to keep productivity and team connection strong?
